epsilon_0.compressed_open: rank of the 96x11 point-ideal matrix is 11
epsilon_0.open: rank(Sub5)=56, i.e. the union of principal opens of its 56x56 minors

epsilon_1.carrier_uniqueness: rank 55 gives a one-dimensional quintic kernel; primality and f3 not in I_C force nonzero F5 coefficient, hence a unique Q2
epsilon_1.compressed_rank_locus: the 96x11 point-ideal matrix has rank 10 and its one-dimensional kernel has nonzero F5 coordinate
epsilon_1.equations_alternative: the 96 binary coefficients of F5_h(c)+F3_h(c)*Q2(c) vanish, together with incidence and rank(Sub5)=55
epsilon_1.rank_locus: I_56(Sub5)=0 and rank(Sub5)=55 (open cover by 55x55 minors)
epsilon_1.restricted_forms: F3_h=h4^3*f3(X0,X1,X2,X3,-(sum_0^3 h_j*X_j)/h4), similarly F5_h with h4^5

carrier_picard_boundary.liaison_does_not_close: negative residual genus for second carrier degrees 6,7 still allows disconnected or nonreduced residuals

degree_five_compressed_point_ideal.columns: the ten substitutions of F3_h(X)*X^beta for |beta|=2, followed by F5_h(X)
degree_five_compressed_point_ideal.epsilon_1: rank 10 and the kernel vector has nonzero F5 coordinate
degree_five_compressed_point_ideal.justification: incidence gives I_C(5) subset I_Z(5)=F3_h*S2 direct-sum <F5_h>, so this compressed kernel equals the full quintic kernel

degree_five_substitution.entry_formula: Sub5[b,alpha]=coefficient of s^(95-b)t^b in product_j c_j(s,t)^alpha_j

incidence_ideal.coefficient_source: the exact cyclotomic integer tensor in universal_marked_family.json
incidence_ideal.equations: E_i,j = c_j(s_i,t_i)-lambda_i*P_i,j(h), for 0<=i<=54 and 0<=j<=3, with the four normalizations substituted
incidence_ideal.warning: expected dimension is not an actual dimension or an emptiness proof

normalized_map_atlas.reason: three distinct ordered marks give the unique PGL2 slice; lambda_0 removes the common scalar of the four forms

qualification_localizations.basepoint_free: complement of the projection of V(c0,c1,c2,c3) in coefficient-space x P1; equivalently the open defined by the saturated elimination ideal ((c0,c1,c2,c3):(s,t)^infinity) intersect coefficient-ring
qualification_localizations.closed_immersion: the open where P1 -> P3 is unramified and universally injective, expressed by Fitting ideals of Omega_map and the residual-to-diagonal ideal on P1 x P1
qualification_localizations.marked_source_distinct: invert product_{0<=i<j<=54}(s_i*t_j-s_j*t_i), after inserting the three normalized pairs
qualification_localizations.multiplicity_one_at_marks: invert the 55 values of the pulled-back cubic divided by the simple source factors at the marked parameters
qualification_localizations.nondegenerate: invert a 4x4 coefficient minor of the four binary forms (open cover over all such minors)
qualification_localizations.note: these are exact finite saturation/Fitting constructions; each is an open cover, not an asserted nonempty condition
qualification_localizations.proper_cubic_intersection: f3 is not in the image ideal

scope.curves_parameterized: closed immersions P1 -> P3 of degree 19 through the 55 ordered sections
scope.descent: the PSL(2,11)-equivariant labelled presentation twists to an F-scheme; an F-point, not merely a geometric point, is required
scope.split_model: the cyclotomic splitting cover of the genuine Schur twist
scope.why_complete_for_target: a geometrically integral curve with Hilbert polynomial 19*t+1 is smooth genus zero; its odd degree-55 point makes the genus-zero curve split over F

smallest_remaining_finite_problem.epsilon_0_test: saturate the 220-equation incidence ideal by the qualification opens and an 11-minor of the compressed point-ideal matrix, then eliminate map/source variables to the h-ring
smallest_remaining_finite_problem.epsilon_1_test: use the 220 incidence equations plus rank 10 of the compressed 96x11 matrix (or the 96 carrier coefficients), require nonzero F5 kernel coordinate, saturate, then eliminate to (h,q) and to h
smallest_remaining_finite_problem.question: does either saturated qualified incidence locus M_0 or M_1 dominate the good hyperplane base, and does its twist have an F-point?
smallest_remaining_finite_problem.required_negative_certificate: a unit ideal or non-dominance eliminant after every stated saturation; unsaturated or modular-only emptiness is insufficient
smallest_remaining_finite_problem.required_positive_certificate: exact F-rational normalized coefficients, source parameters, scales, and q for epsilon=1, followed by independent universal-ideal and residual checks

strict_nonclaims: no point of either marked component is constructed
no actual component dimension is computed
the special carrier Picard group is not determined
no residual degree-two cycle or rational point is constructed

universal_image_ideal.finite_algorithm: bihomogeneous saturation followed by elimination in the displayed rings
universal_image_ideal.validity: on the basepoint-free closed-immersion open this is flat with Hilbert polynomial 19*t+1 and is the universal embedded image

vertical_deformation_at_any_geometric_po.actual_dimension_consequence: the qualified fixed-h locus is reduced and zero-dimensional at every geometric point; the relative qualified projection is unramified, so each component has the dimension of its image in the 4-dimensional hyperplane base (at most 4, and exactly 4 if dominant)
vertical_deformation_at_any_geometric_po.calculation: both summands have degree at most -2; h1=(35-b1)+(35-b2)=34
vertical_deformation_at_any_geometric_po.scope: vertical tangent/obstruction for the fixed hyperplane and fixed 55-point divisor; nonzero H1 is not proof of actual obstruction
